Blocked-by: #14153

The card's own `Blocked-by:` line is correct and verified: #14153 is `pm:dispatched` (in flight, spec seat) and `resolveFlowTriggerKind` lands there. The unlock scan returns this to `pm:queue` when #14153 closes; ⛔ re-verify on the merged tree first — the resolver's shape is what this card consumes.

**Lands in:** `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts` `resolveTriggerBinding` — take `triggerType` from `resolveFlowTriggerKind(flow)` and keep only the per-kind binding construction, with the array-form diagnostic route as an explicit pre-check **before** the resolver (the one deliberate divergence, documented in the resolver's header — ⛔ preserve it, do not "unify" it away). p3: the two chains agree on every string-form flow today and the divergence is pinned; the harm is future drift, where `defineStack` accepts a stack the runtime leaves inert.

Size/model suggestion: S, `opus`.

Round R23. `pm:blocked` → `pm:dispatched` in one label write (read-modify-write, read taken immediately before the write, comparative read-back against `union(current, target)` = `{domain:services, priority:p3, pm:dispatched}` — matched, nothing concurrent stripped).

## Block released — and it had been releasable for ~36 hours

`Blocked-by: #14153` is satisfied: #14153 closed `completed` at 2026-09-02T03:07:20Z via PR #14330. The `domain:spec` seat left a note here the same minute asking this seat's unlock scan to re-verify the file surface before releasing. That re-verification is below.

⚠️ **Nothing put this card back, and that is a mechanism defect, not an oversight by anyone.** This card's line reads `Blocked-by: #14153 (the spec export lands there)` — with trailing prose after the issue number. The lane's other released card today (#14762, on #13881 closing at 09:53Z) carries a clean `Blocked-by: #13881` and was *also* not returned. Found by running the scan by hand: of the 14 open `pm:blocked` cards in this lane, **8 carry no `Blocked-by:` line in their body at all**, so they are structurally invisible to it. Filed as lane hygiene against #14898's body-repair batch; recorded here so the next reader knows this release was manual.

## Premise re-verified on the merged ref — holds, and is easier than the card assumed

Measured on `origin/main` (`git show` / `git grep` against the ref, not against the shared working tree):

| question | reading |
|:--|:--|
| does spec still export the resolver? | `resolveFlowTriggerKind` at `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts:62`, with `FLOW_TRIGGER_KINDS` at `:45` and `FlowTriggerKind` at `:42` |
| did anyone already wire it into the engine? | **no** — zero hits for `resolveFlowTriggerKind` anywhere under `packages/services/service-automation/`, so the defect is intact and the card is not stale |
| is it importable from service-automation? | **yes, via the `./automation` subpath**, which spec's `package.json` declares. ⚠️ It is deliberately **not** on spec's root `index.ts` — a root-index grep returns zero and that zero means nothing. The live precedent is `packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts:106`, which imports it from `@objectstack/spec/automation` in shipped code |
| dependency direction | `@objectstack/spec` is a real `dependencies` entry (`workspace:*`) of `service-automation`, **not** a devDependency — so there is no inversion to work around |
| import site | `engine.ts:3` and `engine.ts:12` **already import from `@objectstack/spec/automation`**. Adding the resolver is one more name on an existing import statement, not a new edge |
| the target | `resolveTriggerBinding` is `private` at `engine.ts:2452`, called from four sites (`:2408`, `:2555`, `:3216`, `:3249`) |

## Scope, per the triage note — the divergence is PRESERVED, not unified

Triage's shape (comment 5503566415) is adopted: take `triggerType` from `resolveFlowTriggerKind(flow)` and keep only the per-kind binding construction.

⛔ **The array-form `triggerType` route stays as an explicit pre-check BEFORE the resolver.** It is a deliberate divergence documented in the resolver's own header — the engine routes array-form to the record-change trigger *so that trigger can refuse it loudly at bind time*, while lint 1d reports the shape itself. "Unifying" it away would delete a standing decision and convert a loud refusal into silence. This is the single most likely way to get this card wrong.

## Where Clause-② could flip, and why it reads `no` today

Declared `no`: no new exported symbol, no new payload key, and no accept-set change — the two chains agree on every string-form flow today, which is pinned in `flow-trigger-kind.test.ts`. The dev re-derives this from its own diff rather than inheriting it, and the one place it can flip is named: if the unification changes what the **public** `getTriggerBindingAudit` or the boot banner reports for any flow — the array-form case above being the candidate — that is an observable behaviour change and Clause-② becomes `yes` with `needs:contract-review` on both this card and the PR.

Size S, `opus`, per triage's suggestion.

## Correction to the claim comment above (5528193593) — the hygiene paragraph was wrong

The release, the premise re-verification, the scope and the Clause-② reasoning all stand. **One paragraph does not:** the claim that "8 of the 14 open `pm:blocked` cards in this lane carry no `Blocked-by:` line in their body at all, so they are structurally invisible to it."

The measurement was body-only. The H4/H19 patrol reads **two channels — body OR comment** (since #10403), because bodies are the riskier write; `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`'s docblock names a body-only read reporting comment-parked lines as absent as a known past error. Re-measured across both channels: **all 8 are discharged in the comment channel. Zero of the 14 are invisible**, this card included — and my hedge about trailing prose after `#14153` was also beside the point, since that line parses fine.

**The actual reason this card sat ~36 hours** is that the patrol is **report-only, exit code always 0**: it reports the finding, and returning a card from `pm:blocked` to `pm:queue` is an action a seat must take. For a `domain:services` card that seat is this one. So the delay is this seat's un-run unlock scan, not a blind mechanism and not another lane's backlog.

Nothing here changes the work: `Blocked-by: #14153` really was satisfied on 2026-09-02, the premise really does still hold on the merged ref, and the dispatched scope is unchanged. Correcting it so the dev does not inherit a false picture of the tooling, and so the next reader does not repeat the body-only read.
